author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Providence man accused of injuring a dog during a disturbance was granted surety bail at his Friday arraignment, according to electronic court records cited by NBC 10. A judge also issued a non-domestic no-contact order in the case.

Police said officers went to a residence on Douglas Avenue on Thursday after a report of a man armed with two knives. The suspect, identified as 47-year-old Shah McKenney, allegedly went inside when officers arrived. During the incident, a dog confronted him and suffered a laceration to its neck, police said. The animal was taken to a veterinarian for treatment. McKenney later surrendered to officers.

McKenney faces charges that include felony assault, malicious injury to an animal, disorderly conduct, obstruction and possession of prohibited weapons other than firearms. The charges are allegations, and the granting of bail does not decide the merits of the case. The court’s no-contact order and bail conditions govern McKenney’s conduct while the criminal proceedings continue. No additional information about the dog’s condition was included in the report.
dek: Police said a dog suffered a neck laceration during a Douglas Avenue disturbance before the suspect surrendered.
headline: Providence man granted bail after disturbance leaves dog injured
